summary.title: 2026 Key Facts at a Glance
summary.smi: Minimum Wage (SMI): 9.55 EUR/hour for part-time workers (includes vacation + extra pay). Full-time: 1,424.50 EUR/month (12 payments).
summary.bonuses: Employer bonuses are applied automatically: 20% reduction on Common Contingencies, 80% bonus on Unemployment and FOGASA.
summary.desempleo: Domestic workers now have full access to unemployment benefits (desempleo), the same as any other worker.
summary.digital: All registration and management is done online via the IMPORT@SS portal using your Digital Certificate or Cl@ve.

whoNeeds.title: Who Needs This?
whoNeeds.p1: If you employ someone to work in your household — cleaning, childcare, elderly care, cooking, gardening — you are legally required to register them with Social Security, regardless of how many hours they work.
whoNeeds.p2: This applies to any regular, recurring employment relationship. Even if someone comes just a few hours per week, if it is on a regular basis, you must formalize it.
whoNeeds.p3: Failing to register a domestic worker can result in fines from 3,126 EUR to 10,000 EUR, plus liability for any workplace accidents.

documentation.title: Documentation Needed
documentation.employer2: CCC (Codigo de Cuenta de Cotizacion) — your employer account with Social Security. See next section if you don't have one.
documentation.employer3: IBAN bank account — Social Security will auto-debit your monthly employer contributions from this account.
documentation.employer4: Digital Certificate or Cl@ve credentials — needed to access IMPORT@SS online portal.
documentation.worker1: DNI or TIE (Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero) with valid work authorization
documentation.worker2: Social Security Number (Numero de Afiliacion) — if they don't have one, you can request it during the registration process
documentation.worker3: IBAN bank account — for salary transfers (recommended but not legally required)

ccc.title: Getting Your Employer Code (CCC)
ccc.p1: The CCC (Codigo de Cuenta de Cotizacion) is your employer registration number with Social Security. You need one specifically for the 'Sistema Especial de Empleados de Hogar' (domestic workers special system).
ccc.p2: You can request it online through IMPORT@SS or in person at your nearest TGSS office.
ccc.online1: Go to IMPORT@SS portal and log in with your Digital Certificate or Cl@ve
ccc.online2: Navigate to 'Inscripcion del Empleador' or 'Solicitud de CCC'
ccc.online3: Select 'Sistema Especial de Empleados de Hogar' as the regime
ccc.online4: Enter your IBAN for SS direct debit
ccc.online5: You'll receive your CCC immediately or within 24-48 hours
ccc.inPerson1: Request an appointment at your nearest Tesoreria General de la Seguridad Social
ccc.inPerson2: Bring your DNI/NIE and IBAN details
ccc.inPerson3: Ask for 'inscripcion como empleador en el Sistema Especial de Empleados de Hogar'

contract.title: The Employment Contract
contract.p1: You must sign a written employment contract. While verbal contracts are technically legal for some arrangements, a written contract protects both parties and is strongly recommended.
contract.indefinido: Indefinite (Indefinido) — No end date. The most common and recommended type. Required if the employment is ongoing.
contract.temporal: Temporary (Temporal) — Fixed end date. Only valid for genuinely temporary situations (e.g., covering a leave of absence).
contract.porHoras: By Hours (Por Horas) — Specifies exact hours per week/month rather than full-time. Can be indefinite or temporary.
contract.key1: Working hours and schedule (e.g., 'Monday and Thursday, 9:00-13:00')
contract.key2: Salary (must meet or exceed the SMI for the agreed hours)
contract.key3: Whether extra pay (pagas extra) is prorated into the monthly salary or paid separately in June and December
contract.key4: 30 calendar days of paid vacation per year

registration.title: Registering with Social Security (Dar el Alta)
registration.p1: You must register your worker BEFORE their first day of work. This is done entirely online via IMPORT@SS.
registration.important: Important: Registering after the worker has already started is illegal and can result in penalties.
registration.step1: Log into IMPORT@SS with your Digital Certificate or Cl@ve
registration.step2: Go to 'Afiliacion, Altas y Bajas' > 'Alta de Trabajador en Empleados de Hogar'
registration.step3: Enter the worker's NIE/DNI and Social Security number
registration.step4: Specify the contract details: hours per month, salary, start date
registration.step5: Confirm your IBAN for the monthly SS direct debit

baseCotizacion.title: Understanding the Contribution Base (Base de Cotizacion)
baseCotizacion.p1: The Social Security contribution base for domestic workers is NOT the actual salary. Instead, the TGSS assigns a fixed bracket (tramo) based on the worker's reported monthly salary.
baseCotizacion.p2: This means your monthly SS payments are based on the tramo base, not the exact salary amount. Here are the 2026 brackets:
baseCotizacion.p3: After you register or update the salary in IMPORT@SS, the TGSS will assign the corresponding tramo. You can verify it on your monthly SS receipt.

monthly.title: Monthly Obligations
monthly.p1: Every month you have three obligations as an employer of a domestic worker:
monthly.obligation1: Transfer the net salary (gross minus worker SS deductions) to your worker. Keep a signed payslip (nomina) as proof.
monthly.obligation2: The TGSS automatically debits both the employer and worker contributions from your IBAN. This happens around the last day of the month for the current month's contributions.
monthly.obligation3: Give your worker a formal nomina each month showing: gross salary, deductions, net pay, and employer costs. Our Nomina Generator tool creates these for you.

vacation.title: Vacations & Leave
vacation.vacation1: 30 calendar days per year (or proportional if less than a full year).
vacation.vacation2: At least 15 consecutive days must be taken together.
vacation.vacation3: The schedule should be agreed between both parties. If no agreement, courts decide.
vacation.vacation4: For hourly contracts with the 9.55 EUR/h rate: vacation is already included in the rate. The worker still gets the time off, but it's already paid for.
vacation.sick1: The worker must provide a medical certificate (parte de baja) from their doctor.
vacation.sick2: Days 1-3: No payment obligation (unless your contract says otherwise).
vacation.sick3: Days 4-15: The employer pays 60% of the contribution base.
vacation.sick4: Day 16 onwards: Social Security pays directly (60% days 16-20, then 75%).
vacation.sick5: You must continue paying SS contributions during the sick leave.

termination.title: Termination & Finiquito
termination.p1: Ending the employment relationship requires following specific procedures:
termination.desistimiento1: You can end the contract at any time without cause, but you must:
termination.desistimiento2: Give 20 days advance notice (7 days if employment < 1 year)
termination.desistimiento3: Pay compensation of 12 days' salary per year worked
termination.desistimiento4: Grant 6 hours/week of paid time for job searching during the notice period
termination.despido1: If there is a valid cause (misconduct, breach of contract), you can dismiss without the 12-day compensation, but you must still provide notice.
termination.finiquito1: Upon termination, you must pay the finiquito which includes:
termination.finiquito2: Pending salary days of the current month
termination.finiquito3: Prorated extra pay (pagas extra) if not already prorated
termination.sepe: Remember to report the 'baja' (deregistration) in IMPORT@SS within 3 calendar days of the last working day.
